StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterDeath.rationale: Right hook. `!wasRemovalPrevented && target == base.Owner && base.Amount > 0` (StockPower.cs:18) maps to powers.py:2972's `creature is not self.owner or self.amount <= 0 -> return`; the replacement carries `StockAmount = base.Amount - 1` (StockPower.cs:23) vs `stock=self.amount - 1` (powers.py:2981) and `ShouldPlaySpawnAnimation = true` vs `respawn=True`; the spawn slot `base.Owner.SlotName` has no sim analogue (slot placement is the monster's record). Checked the 0-amount edge, because power_cmd's step-6 finding (the sim has no 0-amount PowerCmd no-op) would otherwise leave a `Stock(0)` badge the game never shows: monsters/glory/axebot.py:48-51 guards `if stock > 0` exactly as Axebot.cs:78 guards `if (StockAmount > 0)`, so Stock(0) is never applied on either side. The sim's added `self._expire()` matches C#'s CreatureCmd.cs:533 power strip in net effect. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

ShouldStopCombatFromEnding.issue: No sim counterpart. C# reads this through Hook.ShouldStopCombatFromEnding at CombatManager.cs:196, inside the win check: while any power returns true the combat cannot end. `hooks.py` defines no such hook and combat.py:272-277 decides the win purely from `is_gone` over the non-minion enemies. The sim reaches the same OUTCOME here by the mid-death spawn / death prevention described on this record's death entry, which keeps `_all_enemies_dead()` false on its own, so DORMANT -- but the mechanism is absent, and a future power wanting to hold combat open without also adding a creature or preventing a death would have nothing to hook. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.rationale: `wasRemovalPrevented: true` is passed when Hook.ShouldDie returned FALSE, i.e. when the DEATH was prevented (CreatureCmd.cs:566), and `false` on the real-death path (CreatureCmd.cs:519) -- the parameter is misnamed in the decompiled source and is NOT about ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath (computed separately at CreatureCmd.cs:508). So `!wasRemovalPrevented` means "the creature actually died". The sim fires hooks.on_death ONLY on the should_die-returned-True branch (cmds.py:98-105) and fires nothing on the prevented branch, so the guard is satisfied structurally. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

Slot placement is presentation/layout in the sim's model; the Ovicopter egg-slot finding shows the sim DOES model list POSITION where it matters for targeting, and CreatureCmd.add appends here. Flagged as a waiver rather than a gap because a single-enemy replacement lands in the same list position either way.
